patch.value: Release gate omits operational scripts, full-history identities, lint, and duplication

The configured exact coverage gate measures index.ts and series.ts only while three executable TypeScript scripts remain outside instrumentation. release:check has no raw Git object identity audit, and the reachable history currently contains two distinct non-GitHub-noreply addresses without printing their values. No explicit ESLint or jscpd-equivalent gate exists. Publishing must remain blocked until these independent quality and privacy contracts are implemented.

Every executable TypeScript file is instrumented at exact 100 percent for every supported coverage dimension with behavioral tests; ESLint enforces no explicit any, no inline or dynamic imports, erasable syntax, and package conventions; a strict duplicate-code gate runs; a raw physical commit and annotated-tag identity audit includes unreachable objects and permits only approved public identities; tracked files and full history pass secret and private-data scans; release:check and prepublishOnly fail closed on every gate
Inventory emitted sources, operational scripts, all physical Git identities, maintained TypeScript lint tooling, and duplicate-code tooling without printing private values
Makes pm-rl's release-readiness claims literal and privacy-preserving
Prevents operational tooling, duplicated or forbidden code, and historical personal metadata from bypassing publication gates
One fail-closed release command proves all-source quality and full-history privacy
The 2026.8.7 compatibility audit proved the configured two-file gate but found three excluded scripts, two non-noreply history identities, and absent lint/duplication enforcement
pm-rl 2026.7.31 public repository with Node 22/26 CI
Inspect package.json coverageGate.sources and release:check, enumerate scripts/*.ts, and classify unique git author/committer addresses without emitting them
All executable TypeScript and the full physical Git history are covered by mandatory release gates
Only index.ts and series.ts are instrumented; three scripts, raw-object identity privacy, lint, and duplication are ungated
A package could pass release:check while shipping untested operational logic or retaining unapproved personal history metadata

message: Track exact all-source quality and full-history privacy gaps
